thread:
user_acme_cs: FYI we started seeing tool call failures hitting invoice_pdf in prod ~10:40am UTC. error: "schema validation: deadline_ms: integer expected, got string"

erin_support: sorry to hear that — can you paste the failing request payload + sdk/client version?

user_acme_cs: sending sample. we call Redwood via Python SDK v0.12.3. payload snippet:
```json
{
  "tool": "invoice_pdf",
  "args": {
    "invoice_id": "ACME-3245",
    "deadline_ms": "2026-03-17T10:39:50Z"
  }
}
```

jamal_eng: that explains it — the tool schema expects deadline_ms as epoch-ms integer. Looks like the client is serializing a datetime string instead. Is that definitely from the SDK or from your app?

user_acme_cs: confirmed it's coming from Python client. we call: `client.call_tool("invoice_pdf", {"invoice_id": id, "deadline_ms": datetime.utcnow()})` — we assumed SDK would convert.

priya_sdk: which field type is in the IDL for invoice_pdf? I pulled the registered schema: `deadline_ms: int64 (optional)` — so SDK should send int or null. Python SDK used to auto-coerce datetime to epoch ms if you passed a datetime, but there was a change in 0.12.x to avoid implicit coercion. Are you on 0.12.3?

user_acme_cs: yes 0.12.3 pinned in requirements.txt

maria_ts_eng: fwiw we see similar but slightly different behavior from TS client — if you pass a JS Date it serializes to number (epoch ms). Go client currently marshals time.Time as RFC3339 string by default unless using our helper.

nate_go_eng: hi — Go SDK's Marshal for time.Time is standard library -> RFC3339 string. We do provide `redwood.TimeMs` wrapper type in v0.10+ that serializes as int64 ms, but devs often pass time.Time directly.

erin_support: so three different behaviors across SDKs: TS->number, Py->used to coerce but recent release changed to iso string? Go->string. This mismatch causes schema validation to fail and also tool router to choose a fallback tool if arg types don't match.

jamal_eng: can you reproduce locally with a minimal script? If someone posts minimal repro we'll triage. Also can you attach request/response logs from our gateway with x-request-id?

user_acme_cs: attached x-request-id: req_01H8X2Z3KL2; logs:
```
2026-03-17T10:39:50Z ERROR toolcall validation failed req=req_01H8X2Z3KL2 code=400 body={"error":"schema validation","field":"args.deadline_ms","got":"string","expected":"integer"}
```

priya_sdk: quick workaround for Python: explicitly pass int(datetime.utcnow().timestamp() * 1000) for deadline_ms. We'll add a note to breaking changes doc. For long term we probably should reintroduce permissive coercion or provide a TimeMs type like Go. Thoughts?

maria_ts_eng: agree — having a consistent typed wrapper across SDKs is ideal. TS already has `redwood.timeMs(date)` helper in rc.

nate_go_eng: we can mark this as low-severity for Go but it's a UX problem. People expect datetime -> accepted. I can draft a small patch to the Go SDK that recognizes time.Time and serializes as epoch-ms when the target schema expects an integer.

jamal_eng: engineering note: the server-side schema validation is strict and rejects mismatched primitive types. That strictness prevents silent data corruption but leads to cross-sdk friction. We should either: 1) server accept coercible types (string datetime -> parse) for numeric time fields OR 2) SDKs perform consistent coercion based on schema if available. Option 2 preferred for predictability.

erin_support: for this customer's immediate needs, Priya's workaround is best. Also offer to roll back them to previous Python SDK minor (0.11.x) where implicit coercion existed? Are there security/bug reasons they were pinned to 0.12.3?

user_acme_cs: rolling back is possible but prefer forward fix. Can you provide a hotfix or a server-side tolerant parsing until SDKs are patched? Last thing we want is production errors.

priya_sdk: action items: 1) post temporary guidance in support thread & docs (done) 2) patch Python SDK to re-add coercion helper/time wrapper in 0.12.4 (PR in progress) 3) add schema-aware coercion in TS/Go SDKs (tracked) 4) server-side: add a grace parse path for date-strings to integer time fields for next 48h window while clients upgrade — @jamal_eng can you sign off?

jamal_eng: ok to add server-side permissive parse for date-like strings into integer time fields for a short window. Ops: add a feature flag toggle for 7 days and log occurrences. Deploy-bot will kick off canary.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: feature=coerce-dates-to-ints window=48h approver=jamal_eng env=canary

erin_support: I'll tell the customer the short-term mitigation and ETA for SDK patch (48-72h for Python, 1 week for Go/TS wrappers). Also asked them to use explicit int as immediate workaround.

user_acme_cs: thanks all — workaround applied and errors dropped. please keep me posted on SDK releases and server flag removal schedule. :heart:

priya_sdk: will post PR links and release notes shortly. also adding unit tests to catch this across languages.

nate_go_eng: created issue REDWOOD-ENG-872: go time serialization coercion helper + tests.

jamal_eng: closing loop: root cause = inconsistent time serialization across SDKs + strict server validation. fix = short-term server coercion + SDK wrappers + docs. leaving server flag enabled for 48h then monitor logs.`
